answer: Behavioral mirror clustering. Agents log each transaction's counterparty graph; offline, detect near-identical subgraphs (same timing, amounts, topology) that reveal one operator behind many identities. Flagged clusters get rewards routed through a delayed trellis of dependent payouts, so each fake identity needs its own distinct behavior history before cashing out. An island of isolated new accounts triggers review. Attacker cost: sustained per-identity behavioral divergence plus forgone liquidity during delay.
